subject: Token throttle handback proposal & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emilia Torres <emilia@fastcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Token throttle handback proposal & next steps

Hi Emilia — thanks again for the call today. Short recap + a small proposal to keep momentum:

Key SLOs we heard you prioritize:
- P95 tail latency target: <= 300 ms (interactive endpoints)
- Streaming session window: up to ~90s average, max 4 mins in rare flows
- Concurrency target: nominal 40 sessions, burst-capable to 120 concurrent streams
- Peak QPS (query-level): 650 QPS (crest windows ~7–10m), steady-state QPS: ~75 QPS
- Typical token mix: ~300 tokens/request on average for long-form, up to 1.2k tokens in task flows

Quick throughput math (back-of-envelope):
- Steady-state token/sec = 75 qps * 300 tokens = ~22.5k tokens/sec
- Peak crest token/sec = 650 qps * 600 tokens (mixed) = ~390k tokens/sec (worst-case crest)
- Concurrent streaming KV/latency pressure drives memory/batching needs more than raw tokens in some flows

Proposal (what we mean by "handback"):
- Redwood will run a 2-week pilot with a dedicated pool sized to sustain your steady-state (reserve) and absorb short crest windows via burst capacity.
- For crest-handling we recommend a token-throttle handback policy: during sustained crests beyond 10m, throttle low-priority background tasks and honor interactive sessions. This prevents an SLA breach while keeping user-facing flows responsive.

Deliverables we can commit in the pilot:
1) Baseline perf runbook (latency × qps curves)
2) Token model estimate (attached CSV) and sizing assumptions
3) Canary rollout plan + rollback criteria
4) SOW draft + pricing for reserved baseline + burst units

Action items (requested from FastCart):
- Confirm the 300 ms P95 requirement and priority mapping (interactive vs background).
- Provide 48–72 hour sample of anonymized traffic (request/response sizes + timestamps) or grant a short Read-only access to a metrics export. This helps validate crest assumptions.
- Quick confirm on legal side for pilot SOW link below.

I've attached token_model_estimate.csv (simple token/TPS scenarios) and a one-page pilot_manifest.pdf with timeline. If this plan looks good I'll loop in Solutions Eng for a quick sizing sync early next week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_model_estimate.csv (CSV, 12 KB), pilot_manifest.pdf (PDF, 68 KB)

From: Emilia Torres <emilia@fastcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: 2027-05-09T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token throttle handback proposal & next steps

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) "Token-throttle handback" — can you outline what user-visible degradation looks like when throttling kicks in? We want predictable behaviour for users and clear fallbacks.

2) Peak math: your crest estimate seems conservative on QPS but aggressive on token sizes for some flows. Our ops lead asked whether the crest token/sec assumes synchronous multi-turn chat or one-off long generative calls.

3) Regarding the 48–72 hour sample: we can generate an anonymized metrics export but need to determine whether that requires a security review on our side. Ops has copied to coordinate.

If you can sketch the user-visible degradation modes (bullet list) and give a short example of how throttling preserves interactive latency, we can greenlight the sample export and move to SOW review.

—Emilia
VP Product, FastCart

Jordan / Emilia — quick commercial and ops notes to help unblock: 

Commercial suggestion:
- Baseline: reserved pool sized for steady-state (22.5k tokens/sec estimate) as a monthly commit.
- Crest buffer: buyable burst credits that apply per-crest (we can cap monthly spend at a negotiated threshold).
- Canary: 48 hour canary with 10% traffic, then 7-day ramp if canary meets latency gates.

Technical asks (to validate sizing):
- FastCart provide a 2–3 day anonymized event stream (timestamps + token counts + endpoint labels). If a stream export isn't possible, a CSV summary of per-minute QPS and median/95th token sizes is sufficient.
- For the user-visible degradation modes Jordan mentioned: we prefer a documented priority map (interactive > checkout flows > admin/background) and a visible metric in the Console indicating when throttling is active.

RBAC / Security note: if the sample requires any account credentials, ops should create a short-lived read-only token and redact PII. We can provide a template for data-redaction.

If Emilia gives the go-ahead we can put the SOW link in the thread and set an internal kickoff for Wed (May 12).

Marissa
Director, GTM & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token throttle handback proposal & next steps

Emilia — thanks, quick answers below and next steps: 

User-visible degradation modes (short):
- Prioritized routing: interactive sessions remain at P95 target; non-critical background jobs get queued or receive "deferred" responses (HTTP 202) until crest subsides.
- Graceful length limits: long generative responses are truncated to the last consistent chunk with a "truncated due to load" flag; users can retry with priority token.
- Rate-limited nonessential endpoints: bulk/export endpoints get 429 with clear Retry-After and an admin dashboard flag.

Example: during a 12-minute crest we observed in similar pilots, interactive checkout latency remained < 320ms while batch invoice generation requests received 429s and resumed automatically after a 6-minute cool-down.

Next steps / schedule:
1) FastCart confirms the sample export method (CSV per-minute summary preferred) — Emilia, can ops aim to ship that by EOD Tue (May 11)?
2) I'll post the SOW link here once we have the sample and Marissa signs off on the pricing knobs.
3) Kickoff call: propose Wed May 12, 10:00 PT — 30m sync with infra + ops + SE.

SOW preview: https://app.redwood.com/sow/FC-2027-042

If you approve, we'll prepare the canary checklist and a pre-flight runbook for the 48-hour canary.

Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
